description: NaBa₄Al₂B₈O₁₈Cl₃ crystallizes in the tetragonal P4₂nm space group. Na is bonded to four equivalent O and one Cl atom to form distorted NaClO₄ square pyramids that share edges with two equivalent BO₄ tetrahedra. All Na-O bond lengths are 2.59 Å. The Na-Cl bond length is 2.68 Å. Ba is bonded in a 10-coordinate geometry to seven O and three Cl atoms. There are a spread of Ba-O bond distances ranging from 2.78-3.30 Å. There are a spread of Ba-Cl bond distances ranging from 3.15-3.43 Å. Al is bonded to four O atoms to form AlO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two BO₄ tetrahedra. There are two shorter (1.77 Å) and two longer (1.78 Å) Al-O bond lengths. There are three inequivalent B sites. In the first B site, B is bonded to four O atoms to form BO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one AlO₄ tetrahedra and  a cornercorner with one BO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of B-O bond distances ranging from 1.44-1.50 Å. In the second B site, B is bonded to four O atoms to form BO₄ tetrahedra that share  a cornercorner with one AlO₄ tetrahedra,  a cornercorner with one BO₄ tetrahedra, and  an edgeedge with one NaClO₄ square pyramid. There are a spread of B-O bond distances ranging from 1.44-1.53 Å. In the third B site, B is bonded in a trigonal planar geometry to three O atoms. There are a spread of B-O bond distances ranging from 1.36-1.39 Å. There are six inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 150 degrees geometry to one Ba, one Al, and one B atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent Ba and two B atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na, one Ba, and two B atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent Ba, one Al, and one B atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to two equivalent Ba, one Al, and one B atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a distorted water-like geometry to two equivalent Ba and two B atoms. There are two inequivalent Cl sites. In the first Cl site, Cl is bonded to four equivalent Ba atoms to form edge-sharing ClBa₄ tetrahedra. In the second Cl site, Cl is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na and four equivalent Ba atoms.
